title: What If Your Phone Showed Messages From Tomorrow?

shots.vo: Ryan's phone started getting messages. Sent tomorrow.

shots.label: MONDAY, 6:58 AM
shots.vo: It started with one buzz. Two minutes before his alarm.
Unknown number. Sent: Tuesday, 12:14 PM. That was tomorrow.
Sent tomorrow? That's not how phones work.

shots.label: TUESDAY, LUNCH
shots.vo: The next day was pizza day. Ryan's favorite. He ate a salad. Just in case.
Bro, you're eating a salad? On pizza day? Are you sick?
Jake. Best friend since kindergarten. Ate four slices.

shots.label: 12:14 PM
shots.vo: At exactly twelve fourteen, half the cafeteria ran for the bathrooms.
Twelve fourteen. Exactly like the message said.

shots.label: TUESDAY NIGHT
shots.vo: That night, a second message arrived.

messages.text: Bet on the Hawks. Trust me.

shots.label: WEDNESDAY
shots.vo: The Hawks were the worst basketball team in the league. Zero wins all season.
You want to bet the Hawks win? Kid, I'll give you your lunch money back ten times.
The Hawks won by one point. On a shot from half court.
Whoever is texting me... I love you.

shots.label: WEDNESDAY NIGHT
shots.vo: Ryan couldn't sleep. He just stared at his phone. Waiting.
Buzz. Message number three.
But this one wasn't a tip.
Jake. His best friend for eleven years.
The messages had been right every single time.
Ryan gets texts from tomorrow. They've never been wrong. The last one said: don't trust Jake.

shots.label: THURSDAY
shots.vo: Yo, Ryan! You look like you saw a ghost. You good?
Yeah. Totally good. Normal. Very normal.
For the first time in eleven years, Ryan watched his best friend like a stranger.
And Jake was acting weird. Whispering into his phone. Hiding the screen.
No, he can't find out. Not until Friday. Yeah. I'll handle it.
Who can't find out? Me?
Hey Jake. Who was that?
Who? Oh. My grandma. She's... into crypto now.
Jake's grandma died two years ago. Ryan was at the funeral.

shots.label: AFTER SCHOOL
shots.vo: After school, Jake said he had a dentist appointment. Ryan followed him.
Jake didn't go to the dentist. He went to the mall. To the jewelry store.
And waiting for him there was Lily.
Lily. The girl Ryan had liked since ninth grade. And Jake knew it.
They laughed. Then she hugged him. A long hug.
Ryan stood behind a pillar. He felt sick.
Then his phone buzzed.
Message number four.

messages.text: Jake will take everything from you on Friday.

shots.vo: Friday. Tomorrow. Whatever Jake was planning, it was happening tomorrow.
Ryan caught his best friend with the girl he likes. And tomorrow's message says Jake will take everything.

shots.label: THURSDAY NIGHT
shots.vo: Okay. If you're texting from tomorrow... you can read what I send, right?
He typed back. For the first time.

messages.text: I'm trying to save you from the worst day of your life.

shots.vo: Me? I'm texting myself? From the future?
He asked what Jake was going to do. The answer came in seconds.

messages.text: Everyone you care about will be there. You'll lose all of them.

shots.vo: Then tell me how to stop it.
One last text. Three words.

shots.label: FRIDAY MORNING
shots.vo: Ryan! Bro! What are you doing tonight around seven?
Seven. The exact time from the message.
Nothing that involves you. I know about you and Lily. I saw you at the mall.
Wait, what? No, man, it's not what you think. Just come to the gym at seven and—
We're done, Jake. Eleven years. Done.
Half the school heard it. Jake just stood there.
Ryan! What did you just say to Jake? He's crying in the bathroom!
Ask your boyfriend.
My what? Jake is not my... oh my god. You have no idea, do you?
She shook her head and walked away. Ryan felt like he'd won. So why did it feel so bad?
Buzz. A new message. And this one made his blood run cold.

messages.text: Good. Now Lily. Cut her off too.

shots.vo: Ryan ended an eleven year friendship because of a text from himself. Now it wants him to cut off Lily too.

shots.label: FRIDAY, 1 PM
shots.vo: Why Lily? She didn't do anything.
The reply came fast. Too fast.

messages.text: Don't think. Just do what I say.

shots.vo: Don't think. Just do what I say. Ryan read it again. Something about it felt wrong.
I would never say that. I hate when people tell me not to think.
So he tested it. A question only he would know.

messages.text: if ur me. whats the name of my first dog

shots.vo: Biscuit. That's right. Nobody knows that. Not even Jake.

shots.label: FRIDAY, 5 PM
shots.vo: Ryan, honey. Jake's mom just called me. Jake hasn't stopped crying since lunch.
She said he spent all his savings on something for you. For tonight.
For me? What do you mean, for me?
Sweetheart. What's the date today?
Ryan looked at his phone. Friday, the fourteenth.
His birthday. He had been so busy reading messages from tomorrow, he forgot what today was.
The jewelry store. Lily. The gym at seven. It's a party. It's a surprise party.
Jake wasn't stealing his life. Jake was planning his birthday.
Then the phone buzzed. Again.
And for the first time, the message from tomorrow sounded scared.
If the messages were from Ryan... why was he trying so hard to keep himself away from his own party?
The mystery texts aren't saving Ryan. They're isolating him. And they know the name of his first dog.

shots.label: FRIDAY, 5:45 PM
shots.vo: Ryan scrolled through every message. All seven of them. Looking for a clue.
Pizza. Hawks. Don't trust Jake. Cut him off. Cut Lily off. Don't go.
The first two made me trust it. Everything after made me alone.
He typed one more message.
No reply. One minute. Five minutes. Nothing.
Then the typing dots appeared. And disappeared. And appeared again.
Finally, the answer.

messages.text: At the party, you find out the truth.
And I can't let that happen.

shots.vo: The truth about you? You're me. What truth?
Ryan grabbed his jacket. Six fifteen. Forty five minutes to the party.
He ran. And with every step, his phone buzzed. Again. And again.
The messages were getting desperate.
Ryan? What are you doing here? You're not supposed to know about—
The party. I know. Lily, I'm so sorry. I thought you and Jake were together.
Jake? Ryan, Jake was helping me pick a gift. For you. Because I... I like you, idiot.
Ryan forgot how to breathe for a second.
Then Lily's phone buzzed. She looked at the screen. And went pale.
Ryan... why am I getting messages from tomorrow? From you?
Lily just confessed she likes Ryan. And now she's getting messages from tomorrow too.
Lily showed him her screen.

messages.text: I never liked you. Stay away from me.

shots.vo: I didn't send that. I would never send that.
So who did? Who else knows everything about you?
Then Ryan remembered something. Something small.
Three weeks ago, a new kid sat next to him in computer science. Quiet. Always on his laptop.
Ryan had let him borrow his phone. To make one call. Just one.
Owen. The new kid. He had my phone for ten minutes.
Ten minutes is enough to read every message you've ever sent. Every photo. Every note.
Including the dog. Biscuit. It's my password.
But the pizza. The basketball game. How could he know those before they happened?
That was the part Ryan couldn't explain. Unless...
Unless Owen didn't predict them. Unless he caused them.
Who works in the cafeteria kitchen after school? Owen. Who's the Hawks' team manager? Owen.
But why? Why would anyone do all this to you?
Ryan's phone buzzed one more time. The number wasn't unknown anymore.
It just said: Owen.
The messages from tomorrow were fake. A new kid named Owen sent them. And he's at Ryan's party.

shots.label: 6:52 PM
shots.vo: Ryan and Lily ran. Eight minutes until seven.
Jake's in there. Everyone's in there. And I have no idea what Owen wants.
The gym was dark. Balloons everywhere. A huge banner. And fifty people hiding.
Surprise!
You came! I thought... after today... I thought you weren't coming.
Jake. I'm so sorry. I'll explain everything. But right now, have you seen a kid named Owen?
Owen? Yeah. He offered to run the music. Super helpful guy.
Ryan looked up at the giant screen above the stage. It just turned on.
On the screen were Ryan's private messages. His notes. His search history.
Fifty people. Reading every private thought he ever typed. And they started laughing.
Behind the DJ table, a quiet kid smiled.
Owen! Why? I don't even know you!
Owen leaned into the microphone. His voice filled the gym.
You don't know me, Ryan. That's exactly the problem. But I know you. We met nine years ago.
Nine years ago. Ryan was eight. And he had no idea what Owen was talking about.
Owen just exposed Ryan's private messages to the whole party. And he says they met nine years ago.
Owen put a new picture on the screen. A birthday party. Eight year old kids. Paper hats.
That's my eighth birthday. At the pizza place.
In the corner of the picture, a small kid sat alone. Holding a present nobody opened.
I was new in town. My mom made me come. You said, who invited the weird kid? And everyone laughed.
My family moved away a week later. I thought about that party every birthday since. So I came back for yours.
Ryan didn't remember it. That was the worst part. He didn't even remember.
Owen wanted Ryan to feel exactly what he had felt. Alone at his own party.
Fifty faces were turned toward Ryan. Some laughing. Some waiting. This was the moment Owen planned.
Ryan could yell. He could run. Or he could do the one thing Owen didn't plan for.
He walked up to the stage. Took the microphone. And looked straight at Owen.
Owen. I don't remember that day. And that's the worst thing I could say. Because you never forgot it.
I was a stupid eight year old. I'm sorry. I'm really, really sorry.
The gym went completely quiet. Nobody laughed anymore.
He means it, Owen. I know him. He means every word.
Owen's hand was shaking over the laptop. One more button. One more secret ready to go on the screen.
Then he pressed it.
Ryan apologized in front of everyone. Owen had one last secret ready. And he pressed the button.
Everyone looked at the screen. Waiting for the next humiliation.
But it wasn't Ryan's secret. It was a video. Of Owen. Recorded three weeks ago.
If you're watching this, Ryan, it means you didn't run. It means you said sorry.
I made two endings. One where I destroy you. And one where I don't have to.
I didn't want revenge. I wanted to know if you'd changed. You did.
The video ended. Owen stood behind the DJ table, not sure what to do with his hands.
So everything this week was a test?
Owen nodded. He'd wanted to see if Ryan would choose fear over the people he loved.
I did, though. I chose fear. I hurt Jake. I hurt Lily.
And then you came anyway. Even when you were scared. That counts.
Ryan walked over to the DJ table. Owen flinched, like he expected a punch.
Nine years late. But... want some cake?
Owen laughed. A real laugh. For the first time all night.
The music came back on. The party started for real. Jake cried again. Happy tears this time.
Then, at exactly midnight, Ryan's phone buzzed.
Owen was standing right next to him. Phone in his pocket. Not typing.
Unknown number. Sent: tomorrow.

messages.text: That wasn't Owen. Not all of it.

shots.vo: Owen confessed to sending the messages. But at midnight, a new one arrived. And Owen didn't send it.
Owen. Did you send this?
Owen looked at the screen. Then at Ryan. He looked scared.
I only sent five. Pizza, Hawks, Jake, Lily, and the gym. I never sent anything about your dog.
Then who answered Biscuit?

shots.label: SATURDAY, 9:11 AM
shots.vo: The next morning, Ryan sat on his bed. Staring at his phone. One minute before nine twelve.

shots.label: 9:12 AM
shots.vo: At exactly nine twelve, he picked up a pen. And without thinking, he wrote something down.
That wasn't Owen. Not all of it.
The exact words from the message. In his own handwriting. At the exact time.
Some of the messages really were from tomorrow. From him. Helping him the whole time.
Biscuit was me. I was checking that I could still reach myself. That's why it took so long to answer.

shots.label: ONE WEEK LATER
shots.vo: One week later. Ryan, Jake, Lily and Owen. Same table. Every lunch.
So you're telling me future you can text you. And you're using it to... ask about homework?
No. I stopped reading them. Some things you're supposed to find out on the day.
Lily took his hand under the table. Owen pretended not to see. Jake did not pretend.

shots.label: THAT NIGHT
shots.vo: That night, one last message arrived. Ryan almost didn't open it.
Sent: ten years from tomorrow.

messages.text: Thanks for not listening to me.
Say hi to Lily. She says hi back.

shots.vo: If your phone showed messages from tomorrow... would you read them?
